description: RevYield pricing rulebook. Single source of truth for tier economics, contractual entitlements, discount governance and the price-test design. Consumed by data/seed_data.py (data generation) and loaded into dim_tier_entitlements for SQL joins.

experiment.name: FY26-H1 Price Card Uplift Test
experiment.hypothesis: Enterprise demand is price-inelastic enough that a double-digit list uplift paired with tighter discount governance expands gross margin, while Starter demand is elastic enough that the same move destroys it.
experiment.assignment: 50/50 random split at the ACCOUNT level, stratified by initial tier, so a customer never sees two price cards.
experiment.exclusion_rationale: Renewals and mid-term upgrades were grandfathered onto the legacy price card, so they carry pricing_variant = 'not_in_test' and must be filtered out of the elasticity read.
experiment.stratification_rationale: New-business and expansion deals have very different average order sizes. Without post-stratification, a chance imbalance in deal mix between the arms swamps the elasticity signal entirely - on the Starter tier it inverts the sign. Strata are combined using control-arm exposure weights.
experiment.demand_response_note: The modelled demand response acts on contracted volume, not on win rate. Win rates are held equal across arms so the recovered coefficient is an unambiguous quantity elasticity; sql/01 reports win rate per arm as a falsification check.

discount_governance.note: floor_margin_pct is the realized gross-margin floor below which a deal must be escalated regardless of headline discount.

expansion_rules.note: An account is flagged expansion-ready when a weighted utilization score breaches capacity_threshold_pct for sustained_months_required consecutive months.

Starter.elasticity_note: Highly elastic. SMB buyers substitute freely; the tier competes against freemium tools.

Growth.elasticity_note: Near unit-elastic. Mid-market buyers negotiate but rarely walk.

Enterprise.elasticity_note: Inelastic. Deep integration, procurement cycles and switching costs blunt price sensitivity.

segmentation.tier_mix_note: Book-of-business mix, not a headcount distribution. Enterprise is deliberately over-represented relative to a pure lognormal firmographic draw so the price test has enough Enterprise exposure per arm to read.
segmentation.misclassification_note: Share of accounts whose headcount sits in a neighbouring band to their contracted tier - reflects real-world sales judgement and creates genuine tier-migration signal for Phase 2.
